## generic_gather_gen2

**Reproduced teaching defect** in generator SHA `8e723452276e6a8b83fcde1917a0702b13e76989fa2b9d9771c2b0237368dbe2`; no source was changed.

At easy seed `7783`, the supported generator emitted this program:

```racket
(gravity (gravity (recolor g 9 0) "left" 2) "up" 2)
```

The three exposed training inputs contain color 9 exactly `[0, 0, 0]` times, while the query contains it 7 times. Therefore the plausible rival

```racket
(gravity (gravity g "left" 2) "up" 2)
```

fits every demonstration exactly but disagrees with the intended Racket output in seven query cells. The supported `generate` command executed the intended program with rule hash `bb08e02cf8dc`, recorded zero rejections, and saved the exact input, intended output, rival output, differing cells, command, and hashes in `checks/audit/generic_gather_gen2/counterexample.json` and `seed7783.jsonl`.

This is not isolated dead-code noise. Over easy seeds 0..9999, 5,027/10,000 tasks enabled recolor; 6/5,027 had the source absent from every internal training pair, and 2/5,027 also had a source-active query, producing the same train-fit/query-disagreement. Separately, 3,093/5,027 recolor tasks had no source in any test pair, so the optional operation was often query-irrelevant. The bounded probe is `audit_probe.py` with results in `audit_probe.json`; exit 1 intentionally denotes that it found an ambiguity.

`arcpuzzles apply` cannot replay generic seed-specific programs and rejected this target; `racket_apply_console.log` preserves that limitation. I used the supported source-bound `generate` record instead. The exact input belongs to the documented domain because the assigned generator produced it and the supported command accepted it with zero rejections.
